subject: showing more than 6 values in a graph doesn't seem to work

messages.author: f5bec70b36df06aa
messages.subject: showing more than 6 values in a graph doesn't seem to work
parts:
Hi @all

I am sorry to post another problem here but I came across the
following error message (see code below):

Error: scale_shape_discrete can deal with a maximum of 6 discrete
values, but you have 10. See ?scale_manual for a possible alternative

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/
seasonal_var_gw_sixmile.csv") -> seasonal
melt_seasonal <- melt(seasonal, id=c("ID", "date"), na.rm=TRUE)
melt_seasonal$ID <- factor(melt_seasonal$ID, levels =
c(106,107,100,101,125,115,110,112,124,119))
ggplot(melt_seasonal, aes(x = date, y = value, group = ID)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = factor(ID))) + scale_shape(solid=FALSE) +
facet_grid(variable ~ . , scales = "free") + theme_bw() +
opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour="white")) +
scale_x_discrete(expand=c(.005,.005),
breaks=c("2008-10-26","2009-01-27","2009-03-16","2009-07-20","2009-11-16"),
labels=c("26 Oct","27 Jan","16 Mar","20 Jul","16 Nov"))

The only difference to a plot that was working is that this plot
should have 10 ID showing (compared to the one that was working and
had only 6 IDs showing up).

Any ideas what I have to change? It suggested to use scale_manual but
I tried it and it didn't work either.

Thanks
Martin

On Thu, Feb 11, 2010 at 01:29:14AM -0800, waschbaer wrote:
>
> I tried your suggestion and it works in the way that at least it is
> now plotting the graph. However, there are now two legends, one
> showing the points only and the other one showing the lines only. Is
> there a way to merge them?
>

for me it worked when i specified the colour scale manually too:

ggplot(melt_seasonal, aes(x = date, y = value, group = ID,
colour=factor(ID),shape=factor(ID))) +
geom_line() + geom_point() +

labels=c("26 Oct","27 Jan","16 Mar","20 Jul","16 Nov")) +
scale_colour_manual("",values=c("106"= 1, "107"= 2, "100"= 3, "101"= 4,

But i don't know if this is the only solution. I though the same legend
title would merge the two legends, but simply using
+ scale_colour_discrete("") had not effect.

regards,
stefan
